Temporal focus:

T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ September rate hike near-certain; Middle East conflict impact on Japan
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — BOJ rate path to 1.5% by January; sustained yen weakness and inflation pressures

Synopsis:
Japan's Q2 GDP was revised upward to 1.4% annualized (from 1.1%), driven by less-weak capital expenditure. Real wages surged 2.4% YoY in July, the largest gain since May 2021. The BOJ, already at a 31-year high policy rate of 1%, faces strong market pressure to hike further — swap markets price a 98% probability of a 25bps hike to 1.25% in September, with a full hike to 1.5% priced in by January. The Middle East conflict and yen depreciation remain key inflation risk drivers.
